definition: Composite of the named large gadoids, distinguished from dedicated cod, whiting, haddock, saithe, hake, blue whiting and Norway pout groups.
caveat: Table 14.6 additionally places blue ling here. No numerical generic size boundary is stated.

definition: Named small gadoid and rockling species.
caveat: Table14.6 also routes Argentina/Argentinidae here, while section13.44 lists Argentina spp. under SmallDemersalFish. Treat this as a real conflict.

definition: Residual larger demersal and benthopelagic fishes represented in surveys, excluding dedicated groups.
caveat: No numerical size cutoff given. Table14.6 adds commercial catch categories including eels, salmon, seabasses, some pelagic fishes and tunas. Source examples establish actual broad ecological coverage, not a ban on all deepwater taxa.

definition: Residual unspecified small demersal fishes in survey samples.
caveat: No numerical size cutoff. Table14.6 conflicts for Mullus surmuletus and Argentina. Generic marine-fish rows in Table14.6 are historical catch accounting and must not erase named-group eligibility for broad current catch labels.

definition: Residual planktivorous pelagic fishes, with herring/sprat separate.
caveat: Table14.6 also includes capelin, whitebait, Baltic herring, silver smelt and broad other-pelagic labels; whitefish appears in two different groups in the table.

definition: Young spurdog and juveniles of other sharks smaller than 40 cm.
caveat: Length measure is not specified in this paragraph. Juvenile group is not spurdog-only; no measured 2019 caught-mass fraction supplied.

definition: Adult spurdog larger than 40 cm.
caveat: Length measure unspecified in the paragraph.

definition: Primarily tope; porbeagle and thresher are explicitly intended members although absent from 1991 IBTS observations.
caveat: Aloplas is printed misspelling. Table14.6 adds Prionace glauca. JuvenileSharks remains eligible for juveniles.

definition: Named small shark and smoothhound guild.
caveat: Scyliorhinus spelling as printed. Table14.6 adds nursehound/greater-spotted dogfish. JuvenileSharks remains eligible for juveniles.

definition: Skates smaller than 30 cm, across adult skate group identities.
caveat: Length measure unspecified; this does not explicitly say stingrays or electric rays.

definition: Starry ray and unidentified rajid skates.
caveat: Table14.6 specifically assigns shagreen ray and broad Raja/skate labels. Dedicated thornback/spotted and skate/cuckoo groups remain eligible for generic current broad labels.

definition: Adult-group union of thornback and spotted rays based on similar diets.
caveat: JuvenileRays eligible for smaller individuals.

definition: Common skate and cuckoo ray combined.
caveat: Historical Dipturus batis species concept predates split; Table14.6 includes longnosed skate. JuvenileRays eligible for smaller individuals.

definition: Predominantly infaunal bivalves and gastropods greater than 2 mm, plus source-listed infaunal taxa.
caveat: Table11.8 members are PDF118. Do not discard source-listed polychaetes/echinoderms merely because short Table11.6 definition emphasizes molluscs. Buccinium example conflicts with whelk catch crosswalk to mobile epifauna.

definition: Mobile macrobenthos living freely on the sediment surface.
caveat: Table14.6 assigns queen/king/great Atlantic scallops, periwinkles and whelks. Name mobile grazers is narrower than actual source definition, which includes predatory/scavenging taxa.

definition: Small interface fauna, including crustaceans swarming above the bottom.
caveat: Not an indiscriminate all-crustacean pool; dedicated shrimp, Nephrops and large crabs remain separate.

definition: Mainly sediment-dwelling polychaetes and other small infauna.
caveat: Source genera as printed; some are taxonomically or ecologically unusual and are not corrections.

definition: Attached or sessile suspension/filter-feeding epifauna.
caveat: Table14.6 specifically assigns blue mussel, European flat oyster, Pacific cupped oyster. Table11.8 also has named worms; use actual members rather than taxonomy alone.

definition: Modest/large brachyuran crabs recognizable in fish diets and fisheries plus other large decapods, including European lobster and squat lobsters.
caveat: This is not exclusively Brachyura. Small epifaunal crabs can instead belong to mobile macrobenthos.

definition: Norway lobster inhabiting burrows in muddy sediment.
Prawns and shrimps, parameterized mainly using Pandalus borealis and Crangon.
caveat: Diet based entirely on Pandalus borealis; this does not exclude other listed shrimps. Table14.6 includes Aesop shrimp, English prawns and Pandalus spp.
